query: If the ticket types that create the heaviest agent workload were reduced, how much would resolution time drop?

per_column.name: primary_issue_category
per_column.rationale: The query explicitly targets 'ticket types that create the heaviest agent workload.' This column encodes ticket/issue type, which is the lever being reduced. It is a settable/configurable classification an actor could intervene on (routing, deflection, self-service), so it qualifies as the intervenable treatment and is clearly named in the query.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: The agent handling a ticket can influence both which issue types they receive (specialization/assignment) and the resolution time (skill/speed), making it a plausible common cause. It is not named in the query, so it demonstrates the capability under test. However, whether assignment precedes issue type is arguable; it could also be a mediator of workload.

per_column.name: issue_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: A binary severity/urgency signal plausibly drives both the type/volume of tickets (workload) and resolution time (harder cases take longer). Severity is a pre-treatment common cause not named in the query. It is a generic-ish boolean though, weakening its confounding value.

judge.rationale: The treatment (issue/ticket category) is present, intervenable, and explicitly named in the query as the lever to reduce. Two candidate confounders are provided that are not named in the query: assigned_agent and issue_severity_signal. Both are plausible common causes of ticket type and resolution time, satisfying the interventional setup at a basic level. Quality is only moderate: assigned_agent is ambiguous between confounder and mediator of workload, and issue_severity_signal is a thin binary that only weakly captures the true confounding structure (e.g., priority, category already exist in the original table, agent tenure/skill, staffing levels, time period). The set sets up a legitimate what-if but with limited, partly uncertain adjustment coverage.
